metadata.case_name: LI CHEONG KWOK v. UENG TEH CHI FRANCIS

injuries.description: bifrontal subarachnoid haemorrhage with generalised cerebral oedema; severe traumatic brain injury with coma and post-traumatic amnesia
source: bifrontal subarachnoid haemorrhage with generalised cerebral oedema
it is not in dispute that the plaintiff suffered a severe traumatic brain injury with coma lasting at least 5 to 6 days and post-traumatic amnesia.

injuries.description: fracture of the right orbital roof, part of the bony cavity surrounding the right eye, and the right frontal bone
injuries.body_part: right orbit and right frontal bone (face/head)
source: The principal injury was to his face and head where he sustained a fracture of the right orbital roof, part of the bony cavity surrounding the right eye, and the right frontal bone, bifrontal subarachnoid haemorrhage with generalised cerebral oedema, bilateral retinal haemorrhage and left inferior homonymous quadrianopia, and fracture of his central incisors with a deep laceration over the symphysis region of the mandible.
The facial fractures appear to have healed satisfactorily, leaving him with scarring.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple fractures involving skull or facial bones

source: The principal injury was to his face and head where he sustained a fracture of the right orbital roof, part of the bony cavity surrounding the right eye, and the right frontal bone, bifrontal subarachnoid haemorrhage with generalised cerebral oedema, bilateral retinal haemorrhage and left inferior homonymous quadrianopia, and fracture of his central incisors with a deep laceration over the symphysis region of the mandible.
The retinal damage was treated by laser therapy on 12 January 1998.

The principal injury was to his face and head where he sustained a fracture of the right orbital roof, part of the bony cavity surrounding the right eye, and the right frontal bone, bifrontal subarachnoid haemorrhage with generalised cerebral oedema, bilateral retinal haemorrhage and left inferior homonymous quadrianopia, and fracture of his central incisors with a deep laceration over the symphysis region of the mandible.
little reduction in visual acuity but some restriction to visual field in the right eye which the experts estimate to be about a 20% permanent disability in that eye

injuries.description: fracture of his central incisors with a deep laceration over the symphysis region of the mandible
injuries.body_part: teeth and mandible (central incisors; symphysis region)
source: The principal injury was to his face and head where he sustained a fracture of the right orbital roof, part of the bony cavity surrounding the right eye, and the right frontal bone, bifrontal subarachnoid haemorrhage with generalised cerebral oedema, bilateral retinal haemorrhage and left inferior homonymous quadrianopia, and fracture of his central incisors with a deep laceration over the symphysis region of the mandible.
He also lost three teeth, two of which have been replaced by a bridge, and it is expected that he can similarly have the other replaced.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of hard dental tissues and pulp

injuries.description: fractured three ribs on the left side
source: He also fractured three ribs on the left side, his left femur and right fibula.
He also fractured three ribs on the left side, his left femur and right fibula.

The orthopaedic injuries, and the consequential wound infections and deep vein thrombosis, have resulted in permanent swelling in his left leg, the left thigh being at least 9 cm larger than the right, with pain on prolonged walking and in certain weather.
He also fractured three ribs on the left side, his left femur and right fibula.
his fractured femur and fibula were operated on with nail fixation and plating respectively on 20 October.

injuries.description: wound infection over the latter operation sites requiring debridement and skin grafts

injuries.description: deep vein thrombosis in the left leg treated with anticoagulant therapy
source: and his treatment was further complicated by a deep vein thrombosis in the left leg which was treated with anticoagulant therapy.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of unspecified blood vessel at lower leg level

manifestations.description: Unconsciousness and coma lasting at least 5 to 6 days
Loss of memory and power of concentration; problems in learning
Lack of self-confidence affecting his social skills; lacks confidence in meeting people
Personality change: short tempered, irritable and temperamental with his family, moody and depressed
Some restriction to visual field in the right eye (experts estimate about a 20% permanent disability in that eye)
Complete loss of sense of smell and related partial loss of taste
Loss of three teeth (two replaced by a bridge)
Permanent swelling in left leg; left thigh at least 9 cm larger than the right with pain on prolonged walking and in certain weather
Right ankle swelling after sitting for some time
Mild chest pain on coughing or taking a deep breath

Low IQ at the top end of the borderline impairment range; impairments in memory, verbal memory, visual reproduction and associate learning; mild to moderate impairment involving the frontal-temporal region

treatments_received: An emergency operation was performed on the day of his admission to relieve inter-cranial pressure and to suture the facial laceration
his fractured femur and fibula were operated on with nail fixation and plating respectively on 20 October.
He developed wound infection over the latter operation sites which had to be treated by debridement and skin grafts
his treatment was further complicated by a deep vein thrombosis in the left leg which was treated with anticoagulant therapy.
The retinal damage was treated by laser therapy on 12 January 1998.
continued follow-up in orthopaedic, neurological and opthalmological outpatient clinics, as well as physiotherapy and occupational therapy treatment for about two years.
treatments_future: a similar dental replacement every 10 years

losses.description: Some restriction to visual field in the right eye (about a 20% permanent disability in that eye)

Permanent swelling in left leg with pain on prolonged walking and in certain weather

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: Partial impotency and premature ejaculation affecting his sexual relationship with his wife

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public

Prevents him from returning to his pre-accident employment as a container tractor driver
